event.title: UN General Assembly Adopts New Map Reflecting Africa's True Size
event.canonical_title: UN General Assembly Adopts New Map Reflecting Africa's True Size
event.summary: The UN General Assembly has voted to adopt a new world map that more accurately represents the size of continents, particularly Africa. The resolution, initiated by several African nations and co-sponsored by France, received support from 164 member states, with only the United States voting against it. The new map replaces the traditional Mercator projection, which has been criticized for distorting the sizes of countries and continents.

timeline.title: UN General Assembly Adopts New Map Reflecting Africa's True Size
timeline.summary: The United Nations General Assembly has voted to adopt a new world map that accurately represents Africa's size. Sponsored by Togo, the resolution received support from 164 member states, with the United States as the only nation voting against it. The new map replaces the traditional Mercator projection with the more accurate Equal Earth design from 2018.

The new map is based on the 2018 Equal Earth design, which aims to provide a more accurate depiction of global geography.
